Peak Energy Expands Series B Total Financing to $157 Million to Accelerate Manufacturing Amid Growing Customer Backlog
News provided by
Peak Energy Technologies
Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 ET
Share this article

Additional capital will support U.S. manufacturing expansion and commercial deployments beginning in 2027
BURLINGAME, Calif. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Peak Energy , the leading developer of passively cooled sodium-ion energy storage systems for the grid, today announced it has expanded its Series B financing to $157 million, including $132 million in equity financing and a $25 million debt facility from HSBC. The additional capital will accelerate manufacturing capacity to meet growing customer demand and support commercial deployments beginning in 2027.
"Customers are telling us they need a lot more energy storage, and they need better options," said Landon Mossburg, co-founder and CEO of Peak Energy. "That's especially true as data centers drive a new wave of electricity demand. We built Peak to solve the economics of storage at scale, but also to build systems that are easier to live with: quieter, simpler and safer. This capital lets us move faster on both."
Peak initially announced its oversubscribed Series B in October, led by General Motors Ventures with participation from Maverick Silicon, Infinite Capital, Eclipse, Xora Innovation and LG Technology Ventures. With more than $2.5 billion in customer agreements and growing commercial momentum, Peak expanded the round in response to additional investor interest. The new investment will accelerate the company's manufacturing buildout and support a pilot project demonstrating the long-term economic benefits of Peak's technology for data centers. The $25 million HSBC facility will support project deliveries beginning in 2027 and help Peak scale its supply chain as commercial production ramps.
"We're grateful to our existing investors for deepening their support as our backlog grows," said Zack Jacobson, Vice President of Finance at Peak Energy. "Adding HSBC gives us flexibility to fund project deliveries without additional dilution and reserve equity for scaling the business. Building a capital stack that fits each need is how we'll finance Peak's growth, and HSBC is the right partner to lead that."
Peak's flagship passively cooled energy storage system eliminates active cooling systems, requires zero planned maintenance and can reduce the cost of energy by up to 20% compared with conventional storage systems. With systems designed to perform for 30 years without augmentation, Peak delivers significant long-term economic benefits for customers, including data centers with large and growing power needs.
To learn more about Peak Energy, visit peakenergy.com .
ABOUT PEAK ENERGY:
Peak Energy is a U.S.-based company building sodium-ion energy storage to solve today's grid infrastructure challenges. With $157 million in new financing, Peak is ramping domestic manufacturing at its 4 GWh facility in Sacramento, California, to meet growing demand for U.S.-made energy storage. Founded in 2023, the company has over $2.5 billion in commercial agreements, including deals with Jupiter Power, RWE, and Energy Vault, and a strategic partnership with General Motors to develop next-generation storage cells purpose-built for the grid. Chase Properties and Tru Arrow Partners Raise More Than $148 Million Across Two Real Estate Funds
November 24, 2026
Creekside Plaza in Ithaca, N.Y., one of the open-air shopping centers acquired by Fund V alongside TACPP. (Photo: Chase Properties)
Chase Properties , a Beachwood, Ohio-based owner and operator of open-air shopping centers, and New York-based alternative asset manager Tru Arrow Partners have completed the final closings of two real estate investment funds, securing more than $148 million in combined capital commitments.
Tru Arrow-Chase Properties Partners (TACPP) closed at nearly $105 million, while Chase Properties Retail Opportunities Fund V closed at nearly $44 million. Both funds closed within their respective fundraising targets.
Fund V follows a core-plus investment strategy focused on stabilized, income-producing shopping centers, while TACPP pursues opportunistic investments across retail, multifamily and industrial properties, including investments alongside Chase Properties’ retail funds.
Fund V has acquired eight open-air shopping centers alongside TACPP across New York, Virginia, Arkansas, Texas and Illinois, with a ninth property currently under contract.
The portfolio includes prominent national retailers such as T.J. Maxx, HomeGoods, Ross Dress for Less, Dick’s Sporting Goods and Kroger.
“Our investors’ commitments reflect both the strength of open-air retail today and their confidence in how we invest,” said Yoel Mayerfeld , co-chief executive officer of Chase Properties.
“The best centers are in high demand, and pricing reflects that. We’ve owned shopping centers through a lot of cycles since this company was founded more than 50 years ago, and that experience has taught us to be patient and disciplined.”
The fund closings come amid favorable supply and demand fundamentals in the open-air retail sector.
According to Colliers, shopping center vacancy stood at 5.4% in the third quarter of 2026, near historic lows, while CoStar reported that retail construction starts had fallen to their lowest level in at least a decade.
Chase Properties continues to target individual shopping centers and portfolios anchored by national, value-oriented and creditworthy tenants, particularly in secondary and tertiary U.S. markets.
“Our partnership with Tru Arrow has expanded what we can pursue and how quickly we can execute,” said Andy Kline , co-chief executive officer of Chase Properties.
“With both funds closed, we’re actively acquiring, and we want to be the first call from a seller or their broker.”
Glenn Fuhrman , co-founder of Tru Arrow Partners, highlighted Chase Properties’ extensive experience investing in smaller cities and regional markets.
“Having a strong GP that invests its own capital alongside its LPs was a key factor in our investors’ decision to commit to TACPP,” added James Rothschild, co-founder of Tru Arrow Partners.
Founded in 1973, Chase Properties is a vertically integrated real estate investment firm managing more than $1 billion in assets, including approximately eight million square feet of retail space across more than 25 states.
The company primarily invests in open-air shopping centers, with additional investments in multifamily and industrial properties.

News provided by

Nov 24, 2026, 11:00 ET

The combined capital was provided through term loan, revolving debt and convertible note financings to support Harbinger's next stage of growth
GARDEN GROVE, Calif. , Nov. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Harbinger , an American industrial technology platform company, today announced it has closed financing agreements totaling more than $100 million with Erebor Bank , co-founded by Palmer Luckey , and Pinegrove Venture Partners , which is sponsored by Brookfield Asset Management and HRTG Partners. The complementary financing structures include senior debt provided by Erebor and a separate convertible note from Pinegrove.
Continue Reading
Harbinger has secured more than $100 million in financing from Erebor Bank and Pinegrove Venture Partners to accelerate production and support its growing commercial vehicle business.
The transactions mark an important step in Harbinger's evolution from an electric vehicle manufacturer to a broader industrial technology platform company reinventing the critical systems the world depends on across mobility, power, defense, autonomy and components. Harbinger develops advanced electrification technologies, including all-electric and hybrid medium-duty vehicle platforms, battery and drivetrain systems, energy storage and auxiliary power solutions, autonomous driving technology and defense applications.
Harbinger is now scaling production and fulfilling major commercial orders, including its recent multi-year order for 2,000 all-electric trucks from FedEx . Harbinger has added 400 jobs this year, primarily at its Orange County, California headquarters, and plans to continue rapid growth next year, with the goal of creating hundreds of additional jobs around the country.
"Erebor finances companies building the future of American industry—businesses that are making real products, building factories, and scaling U.S. manufacturing," said Palmer Luckey . "Traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and scaling domestic jobs. Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology. We're proud to provide the capital to help build more of America's industrial future here at home."
The debt financing comes on the heels of Harbinger's recently announced Series D funding round, and represents an expansion beyond the equity-driven funding model Harbinger has historically utilized as an emerging technology company. By accessing financing structures more commonly associated with established industrial manufacturers, Harbinger is building a more diversified capital strategy to support long-term growth while demonstrating how a new generation of American manufacturers can finance production at scale.
"Building an industrial technology company at scale requires a different financing approach," said John Harris , Co-Founder and CEO, Harbinger. "The capital needed to ramp production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn't have to come entirely from equity. Major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations, and we're bringing that same approach to Harbinger. articles.text:
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:23 PM
Yreka Western Railroad Secures $60.2 Million Federal Grant for California Freight Modernization
Yreka Western Railroad has received a $60.2 million federal grant to modernize its freight corridor between Yreka and Montague in Northern California.
The award was made through the Federal Railroad Administration’s fiscal 2025–2026 Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements program.
Parent company Railmark Holdings is contributing another $20.2 million in cash and in-kind support, bringing the project’s total value to approximately $80.4 million.
Upgrading the Freight Corridor
The project will upgrade the railroad from FRA Excepted Track to Class 2 standards and allow the route to accommodate industry-standard railcars weighing up to 286,000 pounds.
Work will renew 8.43 miles of mainline and approximately 1.5 miles of sidings and industrial spurs. Improvements include new rail, crossties, ballast and other materials, along with the replacement of 21 turnouts.
Two mainline connections will also be built for the separately developed 58-acre Yreka Rail Industrial Park. The project will redeck the Oregon Slough and Shasta River bridges, replace two short-span bridges with culverts and improve four public road crossings in Yreka.
The upgraded infrastructure is expected to support agricultural producers, lumber and forest-products businesses, fertilizer suppliers, propane distributors, recyclers and building-materials shippers.
Yreka Western connects with Union Pacific Railroad and Central Oregon & Pacific Railroad, providing access to the national freight network. Railmark acquired the historic short-line railroad in 2017.
The project was among 105 selected from 368 applications seeking a combined $12.2 billion in federal support.

SenseNet Raises $43 Million to Expand Wildfire Detection
The Series B financing led by Idealist Capital will fund international growth and commercial team expansion for the wildfire monitoring company.
Updated on Nov. 24, 2026 in Startups
SenseNet has secured $43 million in Series B financing led by Idealist Capital, with participation from Fusion Fund, Stormbreaker Ventures, Thin Line Capital, NBC, and The Sitka Foundation. The company said it will use the capital to scale its international operations and grow its commercial teams.
Why it matters
The financing supports expansion of wildfire monitoring as the company reports tripling its global footprint from 130 million to more than 450 million acres over the last year. The round is expected to accelerate SenseNet's growth in the US and internationally as wildfire risks intensify.
SenseNet's $43 million Series B round includes primary and secondary sales plus debt financing, while its network has grown to more than 5,300 sensors and AI-enabled cameras across 12 countries. The company has not disclosed the proportion of each financing type or its valuation.
The players
SenseNet
SenseNet is a wildfire detection company that deploys sensors, AI-enabled cameras and predictive analytics across multiple countries.
Idealist Capital
Idealist Capital is an investment firm that led the Series B financing round for SenseNet.
The details
SenseNet combines ground-level environmental sensors, AI-enabled cameras, satellite intelligence, drone technology, and predictive analytics into one multimodal ecosystem that integrates with existing third-party and emergency systems without replacing current infrastructure. The company reports US customers including Palo Alto and Woodside fire departments, Santa Clara County and San Jose Water in California, and Jefferson County and the City of Colorado Springs in Colorado.
Timeline
Over the last year: SenseNet tripled its global wildfire monitoring footprint.
During the past wildfire season: SenseNet detected several fires hours before the first 911 reports.
November 24, 2026: SenseNet announced the $43 million Series B financing.
Market Landscape
SenseNet's multimodal approach, which layers ground sensors, AI cameras, satellite intelligence and drones, extends the AI-enabled camera and satellite wildfire detection systems now used by fire departments and water utilities. Its ability to integrate with existing emergency systems positions it as an add-on to current infrastructure rather than a replacement.
Fire departments and water utilities in California, Colorado and other customer regions may gain earlier wildfire alerts through SenseNet's integrated systems. The extraction does not indicate any change to pricing or availability for residents.
The takeaway
Wildfire detection is increasingly being built as layered systems that connect with existing emergency services, which may help agencies respond sooner as fire seasons lengthen.

Native Realty Brokers $35.38 Million Sale of Gateway Shopping District in Fort Lauderdale
November 24, 2026
CEO Jaime Sturgis unites several property owners to close 11-building, 73,756-square-foot retail sale to Miami-based CORE
Native Realty , the Fort Lauderdale-based firm led by Jaime Sturgis , closed the $35.38 million sale of Gateway Shopping District, a 73,756-square-foot retail district located at 1900 E. Sunrise Blvd . in Fort Lauderdale. Miami-based CORE acquired the property.
Native CEO Jaime Sturgis represented the seller, and Native Associate Jeremiah Adler represented the buyer. The transaction closed on Nov. 20.
The sale includes 11 buildings. Only the building at 1990 E. Sunrise Blvd . was excluded from the transaction.
Gateway’s sale marks the culmination of Sturgis’ long-term efforts to revitalize the site through adaptive reuse and thoughtful tenant curation. Gateway was a fractured retail site, with different individual owners holding different buildings within the overall property.
To bring the transaction across the finish line, Sturgis had to secure each individual seller and reconcile differing motivations, timelines and aspirations. He worked to align the group and cross-collateralize the properties so the sale could move forward as a single transaction.
Jeremiah Adler and Jaime Sturgis
“Gateway has always been a site with enormous potential, but its ownership structure made a sale of this scale extremely complicated,” Sturgis said. “Our job was to listen, build trust and find a path that worked for everyone. Seeing this property transform from a neglected shopping center into one of the most dynamic retail destinations in Fort Lauderdale, and then closing a sale of this size, is incredibly rewarding.”
Gateway’s history spans several eras. The site began as a quarry and rockyard before being converted into Jungle Zoo in 1940. It was later redeveloped as a supermarket, then a big-box retail center and, most recently, a boutique neighborhood plaza.
Prior to Native being hired more than five years ago to lease and manage the property, Gateway languished for several decades and accumulated significant deferred maintenance. The center needed new roofs, windows, doors, fixtures, flooring, painting, facades and much more. Native balanced overseeing the complete rehabilitation of the center with simultaneously launching a leasing campaign to attract new tenants.
Sturgis and the Native team reimagined Gateway with a bustling mix of food-and-beverage and experiential retailers, creating a modern retail district that takes full advantage of the site’s highly visible and prime location.
Gateway sits very close to the Galleria Mall, where developer Russell Galbut and his partners are embarking on a major mixed-use redevelopment that will transform the mall into an eight-building destination.
The sale serves as a case study in how Native draws on its vast local market knowledge and relationships to activate a long-dormant asset and position it for a successful exit for the property owner.
